key_insight: RGR moves recursive stochastic gradient estimation into Euclidean space before retracting to the Stiefel manifold, eliminating vector transport and enabling adaptive, horizon-free optimization.
engineering_relevance: This makes nonconvex Stiefel optimization more practical for machine learning systems such as PCA, matrix completion, and orthogonal neural networks by reducing tuning burden and improving convergence stability.
method: RGR-SPIDER: finite-sum variant with Lipschitz-free, horizon-free adaptive stepsizes.
RGR-SRM: online mini-batch variant with no prescribed large batch sizes or iteration budget.
RGR-EMA: online exponential-moving-average variant with similar horizon-free guarantees.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical complexity bounds and experiments on PCA, low-rank matrix completion, and orthogonal CNNs, where RGR variants converge faster than tangent-space recursive methods.
watch_item: The method is specialized to Stiefel-manifold problems, so implementation still requires careful manifold retraction and adaptive-parameter handling.
paper_title: Recursive Gradient Retraction Methods for Stochastic Nonconvex Optimization on Stiefel Manifolds
